name: Plaza and Centro
tagline: The village's entire commercial heart, all in a few blocks
description: The adobe-lined main plaza is the center of everything in Purmamarca: the daily artisan market, the small church, the handful of comedores, and most guesthouses sit within a two-minute walk of it. It is the most convenient base for short stays, though wifi and space fill up fast with day-tripping tour groups around midday.
vibe: quiet adobe village square with a steady trickle of market tourism
bestFor: first-time visitors, short stays, easy walkable access to everything
pros: Easy access to buses and tours
cons: Thin wifi shared across nearby stays

name: Paseo de los Colorados loop
tagline: The red-rock walking trail behind the village
description: A short, well-marked hiking loop that climbs into the striated red and ochre hills directly behind town, with a scattering of quiet guesthouses along its edge. Staying near here favors morning light and hiking access over convenience, since it is a ten to fifteen minute walk back to the plaza's shops and market.
vibe: residential edge-of-village, closer to the hillsides than the shops
bestFor: hikers and photographers wanting quick access to the trail and sunrise light
pros: Direct access to the best short hike in town
Quieter and less touristy than the plaza
cons: Ten to fifteen minute walk to restaurants and market
Even weaker wifi than the centro

name: RN52 approach and lodges
tagline: Highway-adjacent hotels on the way toward Salinas Grandes
description: A cluster of larger hotels and boutique lodges sits along the RN52 approach into Purmamarca, the road that continues up toward Salinas Grandes salt flats and the Chile border. These properties tend to have more reliable power and slightly sturdier wifi setups than village-center posadas, but require a short drive or longer walk into the plaza area.
vibe: quiet highway-edge lodges with mountain views, less foot traffic
bestFor: travelers prioritizing comfort and a base for Salinas Grandes day trips
pros: Better infrastructure and more reliable services
Easy jumping-off point for Salinas Grandes tours
More parking and space for those with a rental car
cons: Not walkable to the plaza market

name: Maimara
tagline: A quieter neighboring village with vineyard views
description: About fifteen minutes south of Purmamarca by road, Maimara is a smaller, far less touristed village known for its striped Paleta del Pintor hillside and small family vineyards. It makes a good alternate or overflow base for travelers wanting the same Quebrada scenery with even fewer visitors and a slower pace, at the cost of even thinner services.
vibe: sleepy farming village with dramatic painted-hillside backdrop
bestFor: travelers seeking maximum quiet and willing to trade convenience for solitude
pros: Very few tourists compared to Purmamarca
Striking Paleta del Pintor hillside views
Cheaper lodging than the Purmamarca plaza
cons: Even fewer restaurants and shops than Purmamarca
Requires a car, remise, or bus to reach Purmamarca or Tilcara
